about: Does a request to judge a named third-party package select research-library? The skill gained
that responsibility on 2026-09-02, with scripts/package_health.py and the criteria section, and
its description had to widen to reach it — the old wording named only the library at
$RESEARCH_HOME, so none of the positives below could have fired on it.
The pair to watch is db-defaults, which owns 'which datastore for this shape of data'. The
boundary drawn here is that db-defaults answers what KIND of thing to reach for and this skill
answers whether a NAMED candidate is fit to depend on. The two negatives are the boundary,
not decoration: a description written as 'choosing a library' would take the datastore case
too, and a suite of positives alone would pass for it.
The last negative is the harder one. It is about a dependency and it is still not this skill:
adding a package that has already been chosen is ordinary work, not an evaluation.
Measured 2026-09-02, candidate mode, 3 runs: 6/7, and the adopted wording won 9 of the 12
fires against its own incumbent twin. The three positives the widening was written for went
3/3 each and the clone case correctly stayed with the incumbent, which is the adopt test.
The py.typed case failed 0/3 and is KEPT rather than reworded. It names no package and no repo
— 'does this package ship py.typed' reads as a generic typing question, and the description is
deliberately scoped to a NAMED candidate. It is the boundary seen from the inside, and a suite
that only holds cases the description already wins measures nothing.

cases.prompt: We're about to depend on aiogram. Is anyone still maintaining it, or is it one person?
Before I add httpx to pyproject.toml, check how often it actually releases and whether its test suite is real.
Does this package ship py.typed, and how much typing work are we going to inherit from it?
python-telegram-bot caps pydantic below 2.14. Is that cap going to hold us back?
Clone the anyio repo into the research library so I can read its source instead of the docs.
We need somewhere to keep session state that survives a restart. What kind of datastore fits?
Add the pinned version of requests to this project's dependency group and lock it.
